saurabh: Heads-up — ran the attention kernel seq/batch sweep across H100/A100/L40S this morning. Seeing a regression only on L40S with FlashV2 when KV cache is enabled: ~15-25% lower tokens/sec at seq=512, batch=8. Not seeing the hit on H100/A100. :thinking:

alex: Can you paste the exact bench command you used?

saurabh: Sure — full command I ran locally on the L40S node:```
./run_attn_bench --model=gpt2 --gpu=L40S --seq=512 --batch=8 --kv-cache=on --variant=flashv2 --iters=2000 --warmup=200
```

perf-bot: Auto summary: FlashV2 (kv=on) L40S seq512 b8 = 12.1k tok/s; baseline FlashV1 L40S seq512 b8 = 15.0k tok/s; H100 FlashV2 seq512 b8 = 37.2k tok/s (no regression). p99 latency increase from 12.8ms -> 16.7ms on L40S.

jen: Do you have a profiling flamegraph / NVTX trace for the bad run? Could be kernel fallback / memory thrash.

saurabh: Uploading trace now — nvprof + nvtx collected and pushed to S3: s3://redwood-perf/trace/1749876543/l40s-flashv2-kv-on-trace.html :link:

marta: Quick thought — when kv-cache is on, our paged allocator can cause more small-page eviction/rewinds on L40S due to different page size / TLB behavior. That combined with the new write-prefetch in FlashV2 could be generating extra syncs. Try toggling prefetch or use manual prefetch strategy.

alex: Can we reproduce with a microbench that isolates the fused kernel (no IO/allocator noise)? Something like `kernel_microbench --variant=flashv2 --seq=512 --batch=8 --kv-sim=on`

saurabh: Did a quick microbench with isolated kernel (same box):```
./kernel_microbench --variant=flashv2 --seq=512 --batch=8 --iters=1000 --tile=64
```
Result: microbench shows ~18% slower than expected and shows frequent kernel relaunches in the trace (small 1-2ms kernels).

perf-bot: Profiling highlights: top kernel time: fused_flashv2_kernel (60%), paged_attn_spill_handler (18%), cudaMemcpyAsync stalls (7%). Observed increased kernel launches per token compared to baseline.

marta: Sounds like kv-cache eviction causing page-swap hotspots + kernel split into smaller launches. Try `--kv-cache-strategy=manual_prefetch --prefetch-pages=4` to force larger continuous pages into GPU memory and reduce eviction thrash. Also test lowering tile size to 32 which helps L40S memory access patterns.

saurabh: Tried manual prefetch + tile=32. New numbers: FlashV2 L40S seq512 b8 = 14.3k tok/s (close to baseline), p99 down to 13.5ms. So toggling prefetch fixed most of it.

jen: Nice. That confirms allocator/prefetch interplay. Next steps: bisect patches merged in the flash-attn branch since last green. Could be a prefetch change or kernel tiling heuristic tweak.

alex: Proposed bisect plan: 1) run quick binary search of commits between 2026-01-15..2026-02-02 on a CI L40S worker with the exact microbench (seq512 b8 kv-on). 2) If commit points to kernel change, run small reproducer with `nvtx` to see which kernel split shows up. I can script the bisect.

eng-runtime-bot: Scheduled job created: job-id=er-1749877-bisect, target nodes=L40S-canary-2, command=`kernel_microbench --variant=flashv2 --seq=512 --batch=8 --kv-sim=on --nvtx` — ETA 25m.

marta: If bisect implicates allocator layer, we should add a regression test that runs seq512/b8 with kv-on on L40S in our nightly perf suite.

saurabh: Agreed. I'll add the perf test and follow the bisect results. Assigning action items: @alex to run bisect script, @marta to add perf test, @jen to keep an eye on rollout gating for FlashV2. :thumbsup:

alex: On it, starting bisect now. Will post earliest bad commit. :eyes:
